topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological Nature of Cancer and Mutational Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explain how endogenous and inherited processes drive the accumulation of cellular mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the 'Bad Luck' versus Extrinsic Risk Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate whether cancer risk is driven primarily by environmental exposures or random intrinsic bad luck through everyday examples, public debate, and global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: DNA Damage Mechanisms of Chemical Carcinogens and Radiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens—often activated through xenobiotic metabolism—inflict DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic aspects of carcinogenesis, showing how tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk–Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary of the lecture, reflecting on environmental cancer causation and individual risk–benefit decisions.
